svg.title: PCCR parallel architecture with N agents and N tasks
svg.desc: Complete architecture showing parallel task queue, per-task working memory, DAG-based parallel agent groups, PCCR rho-gate routing, shared memory stores with access controls, and staging-merge pattern
svg.text: PCCR + parallel architecture
N parallel tasks × N parallel agents per task
Each task runs its own 10-phase lifecycle independently
Expanding Task 1 below to show internal parallel agents

g.text: PM + WM always | STM check | ρ = utility/cost ≥ θ → consult store
Independent subtasks → same group, dependent → next group

svg.text: no deps
depends on G1

g.text: More groups? → back to orchestrator. Done? → Phase 9

svg.text: W1: success gate
W2: pattern → STM (atomic write with lock)
W3: person → ENT (lock per user profile)
W4: experience → EM (deferred)
W5: rule → PM (deferred)
W6: routing history (atomic)

g.text: WM CLEAR (this task's WM freed for next task)
No tasks running. EM + SM + PM + STM batch writes.
Trajectories → EM/SM (FAISS). Episodes → PM (learned rules). Training → STM.

svg.text: Key design decisions
Parallel tasks: each gets own WM instance. No cross-task WM conflicts.
Parallel agents: frozen WM snapshot + per-agent staging → merge after group.
Dependency DAG: independent subtasks → same group (parallel), dependent → next group.
ρ-gate: runs ONCE per task in Phase 3, before any parallelism. No changes needed.
Shared stores (STM, EM, SM, ENT): atomic ops / locks for parallel task writes.
Consolidation window: Phase 10 is exclusive — no tasks during FAISS writes.
Inspired by: DynTaskMAS (SACMS), GAP (DAG), SPOQ (waves), CompArch (consistency).
